result.title: Prune to Expand: Training Prompt Enhancers with Less to Imitate
result.summary: Prompt enhancement (PE) refines concise user prompts into detailed descriptions to improve the compositional aesthetics of generated images while preserving user intent. A common practice constructs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) pairs by deriving short, user-like prompts from dense captions, implicitly assuming that captions that improve image generation also provide effective supervision. In this paper, however, we uncover a counterintuitive finding: PE models trained on caption pairs with substantial generation gains perform comparably to those trained on pairs with only marginal gains. We argue that dense captions can impose redundant supervision by requiring PE models to reproduce image-specific details weakly related to user intent. Motivated by this discrepancy, we introduce Prune to Expand (P2E), a simple text-only method that refines dense-caption supervision by selectively removing redundant sentences under a per-example deletion bound while preserving explicit user requirements and informative visual structure. Extensive experiments under identical training configurations demonstrate that P2E improves alignment with human preferences and visual quality over conventional dense-caption SFT across diverse image categories and visual generators.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究 prompt enhancement 的监督数据构造，发现用密集 caption 派生的训练对，其图像生成增益大小与最终 PE 模型效果并不对应，据此提出纯文本方法 P2E，在每例删除上限内筛除与用户意图弱相关的冗余句子来精炼监督。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「冗余监督稀释有效信号、逐例裁剪监督句」的做法可能可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中哪些视觉细节监督真正贡献学习信号；但论文任务为图像生成提示改写，与视觉推理状态无直接联系，迁移性待判断。
